correctness.rationale: For fixed color of a potential parent, exactly four boundary triples are possible. Induction proves each message counts each subtree coloring once, subject to genuine witnesses for all white descendants. A white vertex can be witnessed by a black child precisely when that child has no white children; a black vertex can resolve pending white children precisely when its total number of white neighbors is one. The displayed transitions encode both conditions including the external parent bit; the root excludes imaginary witnesses and components multiply. The tree recurrence therefore covers all orders, rooted shapes, isolated vertices and the empty forest. The packaged verify_forest.py and verification_output.txt report 3,363,980 direct candidate-subset comparisons in 1842 instances (1442 labeled trees plus 400 seeded forests), as well as matching-degree and relabeling checks. Finite tests support but do not establish the general induction. Polynomial complexity follows from four triples times two parent colors and twelve running aggregates with capped white-child count.

value.rationale: The starting 2022 primary paper explicitly requests the count of minimum super-dominating sets in arbitrary trees. This theorem calculates that natural counting question and much more: the entire distribution for each forest, with an explicit practical constant-state recursion and no restrictions on maximum degree or connectedness. The need to distinguish pending white children and a possible future witness from a black child makes it more than a renaming or direct scalar substitution. A prior general MSO result gives abstract tractability but not this concrete state structure or immediately usable coefficient formula. No optimal-state or unrelated downstream theorem is claimed.
